Variants.Content: Qarkash is located to the west of Qarth and the Jade Sea trade route. Politically, it is within the area where Qarth merchants communicate with the towns on the eastern edge of Gith. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry Qarkash Local families also relied on wells, camel caravans, spices, and supplies across the Red Waste; if any road, well, or dock failed, the cost would fall first on them.

Entry Qarkash Quekaxi is located in the power and trade network in the eastern border of Qarth, and the rules inside and outside the city gates are determined by local order; whether the defenders are well fed and whether reinforcements can arrive on time are more important than the rhetoric in the meeting hall in determining whether this stronghold is reliable.

Entry Qarkash They will also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the eastern lands of Qarth; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, and true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Qarkash Quekaxi is located in the power and trade network in the east of Qarth, and the rules inside and outside the city gates are determined by the local order; after the flag is changed, the roads, granaries, old debts and local trusts still have to be taken over by the new owners one by one.

Entry Qarkash If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The craftsmen used their hands to measure the workshops, markets, roof tiles, church bells, and alleys of Quekasi. The priests used rituals to continue the memories of the gods of Qarth, the merchant king, and the burial customs in the wasteland. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Qarkash They care about water wells, camel caravans, spices and supplies across the red wasteland. They also look at whether seeds are left behind after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
